sheets.prompt:
Create ONE six-photograph CONTACT SHEET for choosing a quiet photographic BACKGROUND for the "Growing Techniques" section opener of a British vegetable gardening book.

IMPORTANT ART DIRECTION: The user discovered that a giant hero tomato drew too much attention. They prefer the continuous leaf textures of leeks and cabbage. These NEW photographs must distribute interest around each portrait frame. There should be no one spectacular fruit, flower, large tool, central object, isolated seedling, person or hand attracting the whole eye. Use natural repeated planting, varied leaves, soil texture and subtle cultivation details, with enough photographic depth to feel real. Each image should read as a whole garden texture or small scene rather than a product portrait. This is background selection BEFORE page layout: no headline, contents oval or typography over the pictures.

Reference 1 supplies ONLY the six-panel sheet FORMAT and natural photographic quality, NOT its hero-subject compositions.
Reference 2 is the actual greenhouse: use its honest weathered timber staging, ordinary pots, aluminium glazing and informal growing conditions for greenhouse material/atmosphere. Crop tightly so no conspicuous roof, bright sky, buildings or large pot dominates.
Reference 3 is the actual allotment: use its crumbly dark soil, ordinary irregular young plants, slender natural canes, modest beds and mesh textures. Crop out sheds, labels, houses and sky. These are proposed seasonal/detail studies informed by these real garden references, not a documentary exact view of the whole site.

FORMAT: exactly SIX equal PORTRAIT photographs in 3 columns x 2 rows. Each photo about185:240 ratio. Nearly square landscape sheet around1320x1194 or larger. Narrow warm-white gutters and separate number strips BELOW each photo. Top row numbers1,2,3; bottom row4,5,6. Plain black numerals are the ONLY text.

1 — PLANTING OUT: Close oblique view across a group of young brassica transplants established in crumbly garden soil, perhaps twelve small blue-green plants at varied sizes and angles in loose staggered rows. Look across them, not into a single plant. Leaves and soil fill the frame, with natural gaps and diffuse soft daylight. No giant foreground seedling, hand, labels or tool.
2 — SOWING ROWS: A gentle diagonal rhythm of shallow seed drills in well-prepared dark soil, with modest uneven rows of just-emerging vegetable seedlings in two neighbouring drills. The soil texture, short green shoots and diagonal lines share attention. Edge-to-edge intimate garden detail; no isolated prominent seed, no perfect computer-straight grooves, no overhead teaching diagram.
3 — COMPOST MULCH AND GROWTH: Low oblique view across a mulched leek bed, several young-to-middle sized leeks with overlapping blue-green leaves at varied angles, dark crumbly compost visible between them. Balanced patches of foliage and soil throughout, no hero leek bulb. Organic informal planting, gentle daylight, touch of warm soil texture. Distinct from the brassica seedlings and seed-drill scenes.
4 — PEA SUPPORT: A softly layered screen of healthy pea leaves, several fine tendrils and unobtrusive ordinary green support mesh. Leaves of varying sizes overlap through the frame. A few short slim pods may appear discreetly in different places, none a hero. Natural green-on-green pattern, subtle depth, no large blossom or conspicuous poles.
5 — CROP PROTECTION: Close garden view along a low area of fine white insect-proof mesh over blue-green young brassica foliage, the plants clearly discernible beneath and mesh gently curved. The netting is a light fine texture, not huge foreground fencing; no dominant frame or knot. Fill the portrait with repeated foliage and protective mesh, quiet shade/diffused light, no bright white blank sky.
6 — STARTING PLANTS UNDER COVER: A diagonal close-to-medium view along a greenhouse staging area containing several small trays of young leafy vegetable seedlings in dark cells. Plant heights and leaf directions vary, a few spaces are empty. Repeated foliage/cells form the image's rhythm. Weathered wood and faint glazing lines set the place at edges only. No coloured labels, writing, giant individual pot or single prominent plant.

ALL SIX: convincing natural editorial photography, authentic small British garden scale, gentle overcast/diffused light, natural moderately muted greens, olive and earth tones, midtone/deeper greens across much of the upper area for a later white title. No artificial gradient, tinted overlay or blank reserved typography space now. No HDR, glamour lighting, artificial perfection, identical cloned plants, symmetrical staging, staged tools or arranged harvests. Keep most plants healthy, modest real imperfections only. Botanical forms and attached leaves/stems should be credible. Some soft background depth is welcome, but enough detail across the frame for engaging background texture. Different compositions and camera distances across all six, cohesive restrained style.

Create ONE six-photo contact sheet, the second sheet of background choices for the Growing Techniques section opener of a British gardening book. EXACTLY SIX portrait photos in a 3-column by 2-row layout, matching reference1: equal185:240 portrait frames, narrow warm-white gutters, separate number strips underneath. Top row7,8,9; bottom row10,11,12. Only those six black numerals as text. No book titles, contents, oval overlays, labels inside photographs or borders within the images.

NEW USER REQUEST: include JOHN as an actor in SOME photographs, but IN THE BACKGROUND. Photos7,8,10,11 include him working candidly behind foreground planting. Photos9,12 have no person. The garden remains the dominant visual texture. Do NOT turn John into a portrait subject or a large foreground gardener. Place him several metres behind the nearest plants, usually in the upper-right/middle background, about25–35% of the photograph's height (a crouched body can be smaller), around15–22% of its width. His muted clothing should blend with the garden. He must remain recognisably the man in the camera references but slightly softer than the foreground foliage, not a faceless blob. No camera eye contact, smiles, posing or waving.

REFERENCE ROLES:
1 — first Growing Techniques contact sheet: exact panel format, restrained photographic colour and background-based visual approach.
2 — actual John photograph in summer clothes: likeness, age, mature body/build, high/receding forehead, short greying hair at sides, modest grey beard, olive T-shirt and olive shorts. Bareheaded. Remove the microphone, held hat and presentation gesture. Muted T-shirt; do not reproduce readable clothing text.
3 — actual lowered-profile reference sheet: use the first THREE real camera stills for face anatomy, NOT the fourth generated illustration. The hats/coats here are NOT the wardrobe.
4 — actual allotment: dark soil, ordinary small beds, grass/paved edges, young plants, modest allotment scale. Use close crops of this setting for outdoor work, excluding sheds, houses and bright sky.
5 — actual greenhouse: glazing, weathered staging, brick bed edges and aisle; use its materials and plausible working space for photo11. Preserve small domestic scale.

CRITICAL JOHN LIKENESS: His lower lip sits visibly ahead of his chin when looking down. The short beard slopes back towards his throat. Do not add a protruding rounded beard, square jaw or jutting heroic chin. Maintain real forehead, nose and natural middle-aged/older appearance from actual photographs. No beautifying or rejuvenation. Keep head turned modestly down-left in the working scenes. Hands and tools must connect correctly and have plausible anatomy and weight.

7 — PLANTING OUT, JOHN BEHIND THE BED. Camera at low plant height, foreground and middle ground filled by varied small leafy vegetable plants and dark compost in diagonal loose rows, enough differently sized leaves to create distributed texture. At the far edge in the upper-right background, John kneels beside the bed on a narrow path, looking down-left as he gently firms soil around a small transplant with one hand, the other supporting his balance. He is a small secondary worker, not foreground, and his planted stance/knees are believable. Dense modest green planting surrounds the action; no single huge cabbage or central showpiece.
8 — WATERING, JOHN SET BACK. Different garden view across a leafy salad bed, softly varied greens filling lower two-thirds. John stands well behind, upper-right background, leaning slightly down-left with an ordinary modest green watering can. Hold handle correctly; short gentle flow from rose goes down to soil at plant bases nearby, not a spectacular arc across the photograph. Can and hands are also in the background. His clothing/figure harmonise with the green scene, foreground leaves and earthy gaps share the eye's attention.
9 — MAKING AND USING COMPOST, NO PERSON. Intimate oblique view of rich mature compost with an uneven crumbly surface, modest fragments of brown leaf material and tiny woody bits; a weathered timber edge runs quietly along one side and a little soft green garden growth appears along the far margin. Natural tactile brown/olive/green textures spread throughout, no enormous heap against sky, no worms as hero subjects, no brightly coloured raw kitchen scraps, no pitchfork or staged objects. This is a quieter earthy alternative.
10 — PREPARING A BED, JOHN IN THE DISTANCE. Camera looks low across a modest freshly raked soil bed edged by patches of growing vegetables, with rich fine soil and repeated little plants in foreground. John stands on the far path in the upper-right background, body aboutone-third picture height, looking down-left while drawing an ordinary wooden-handled metal garden rake through the surface. Both hands naturally grip the handle at different heights; rake head sits on soil near him, not at the camera. Do not show him standing on the planted bed. Keep the gesture candid and small; crop out buildings/sky.
11 — GREENHOUSE TENDING, JOHN BEHIND FOLIAGE. Layered mid-green leaves and the natural rhythm of several ordinary planted pots and weathered staging lead into the small greenhouse. John is at the farther part of the aisle, upper-right background, about30% picture height, partly occluded below waist by foliage, looking down-left and gently checking a small potted plant on the bench with his hands close to the plant. Use reference5's greenhouse character and brick/paved aisle. No giant foreground fruit, no portrait framing, no bright empty roof area. Green-on-green natural depth, user recognisable yet unobtrusive.
12 — PLANTS READY TO GO OUT, NO PERSON. Closer oblique pattern of overlapping small vegetable seedlings in a loose group of ordinary reused dark and muted terracotta pots on a weathered greenhouse bench, leaves varied in size/lean, plants not cloned, some dark compost visible between stems. Crop partly through the pot group so there is no one central hero pot and no perfectly arranged still life. Green leaf texture carries across the whole portrait. No labels or writing.

ALL: real-looking editorial British garden photography in soft overcast/diffused daylight, natural texture, muted greens and earth, no HDR or cinematic grading. Interest spread around each image instead of a prominent single subject. Natural imperfect informal growth, no identical repeated leaves or symmetrical grids. Avoid over-blurring entire backgrounds: action should remain understandable. Photos are standalone background candidates; no page typography now. The people are deliberately secondary.
